Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1445. Striker Che Adams says Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is big on the small details... 'he loves his FaceTime calls'

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be big on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the new man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli

Striker Adams says Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’

John McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

‘He said to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very important to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ said Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’

#1444. Q&A: Armstrong On Everton DNA & Breakthrough Season

Q: Harrison you've enjoyed a breakthrough season, earning regular football here at Everton. What's it like to be here right now?

It’s difficult to say it’s everything you think it’ll be because it’s a lot of hard work, and it’s a lot of maintaining everything you’d probably expect. You need to maintain your levels every day, when people watching and when they aren't watching, too.

It’s really good and I’m really enjoying where I am at the moment. It’s where I’ve wanted to be since I was a little boy. I’m just trying to cherish it.

Q: Now that you’re here, does it feel like what you expected?

A little bit but in different ways. I think there are some things – like playing in front of however many thousands of fans – that you can probably expect what they feel like. It’s the best feeling. I haven’t scored in front of the fans yet, which could probably top that.

But listening to Z-Cars when you come out, and even the away games – the away fans and the amount of noise they make – it’s a unique feeling.

It’s only something you can understand when you’re in that moment. And it’s the best.

Q: When you’re playing, is there still that young lad stood in the crowd at the foremost of your mind?

Yeah, definitely. There are moments where you’re coming up against players who I’ve watched since I was young.

Even playing with players. Not that long ago, I was sat on the couch at home watching Jack (Grealish) in the Champions League.

To say they’re my teammates now is surreal, really. But I think it’s a feeling you’ve got to manage at times – managing the balance of respecting them, but also proving yourself and showing what you’re capable of.

I’d say moving away from home for my first loan to Derby. That was difficult in a good way. It was challenging living at home on my own.

Having to cook, but maybe not so much cleaning! It was a challenge, but, looking back, it was definitely something that propelled me forward as a human more than anything.

Having to meet new people in a different environment and build those friendships and relationships with staff and having to do that quickly was a challenge, but I’d say I took to it well. Going in and not playing straight away was probably the best thing for me. It didn’t feel it at the time, but it let me settle in and get used to my surroundings.

Yeah, I’d say so. I think sometimes when I hear people say about how mature I am, I don’t really believe that! I don’t think they’ve seen the other side to me.

I think it’s important I just enjoy what have in this moment. I know that, hopefully, in a few years when I’ve had a long career, I’ll be looking back on this and wishing I was back to where I am now.

Q: You must be delighted having the start to the season you’ve had, playing and starting every game and be able to show what you can do?

Yes, but there’s definitely things I can improve on. I’m happy with where I’m at, but I definitely want to push on.

I want to improve on goals and assists and influencing games more. I know from playing football since I was young and being here since the age of four or five, I’ve seen different parts of my game and how I can draw it out more.

To do that in the best league in the world is difficult, and at times, you’ve got to respect that you’re playing with some of the best players in the world and coming against some of the best opposition.

But I think there are definitely more levels for me to go to. To do that, I have to do the basics wells, but also be myself, take risks and not be too bothered about not getting it right every time.

Q: How is the manager helping you do that?

He gives 100 per cent trust in me. I think the fact I’ve started every Premier League game this season shows that.

He’s someone who has been in the game a long time and has worked with some of the best English players to have come through. To have someone like that with so much experience and so much to learn from is really important.

The trust he’s shown in me, I’m really grateful for.

Yeah, really demanding. I think sometimes I’ll come off and I think I’ve played better than what he thinks! But it’s a good relationship. He knows how to get the best out of me, how to push me. Hopefully, we can do really good things.

Sometimes that’s what you need, isn’t it? To keep your feet on the ground and I understand what you need to do to improve.

I think that’s almost part of Everton’s DNA – not getting too high and not getting too low. I think it’s a club that’s very demanding of hard work and staying ground – and he definitely applies that.

Q: You’re someone who has been here a long time already – through the Academy and now the first team. In your opinion, what does it take to be an Everton player? And how does it differ to other clubs?

It definitely takes a lot of hard work, especially in the tough moments. The city and the environment I grew up in, you had to find out for yourself – you were in the deep end.

You had to show your ability and show what you’re made of. I keep going back to it, but Everton’s a club where you have to do the basics very well first and foremost, then prove your quality.

#1443. Spurs finally score... but still lose

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”

Rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P

Is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo said.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1442. Jake O’Brien Inspires Young People Living With Type 1 Diabetes

Everton defender Jake O’Brien joined schoolchildren living with Type 1 diabetes at Finch Farm for a workshop delivered by Everton in the Community (EitC), sharing his own experiences of the condition after being diagnosed at the age of 16.

Ahead of World Diabetes Day on Saturday 14 November, the Republic of Ireland international met pupils and teachers from local primary schools as part of the charity’s ongoing work to improve awareness and understanding of Type 1 diabetes and create more supportive environments for children living with the condition in schools.

Pupils from five of EitC’s Premier League Primary Stars and Steve Morgan Foundation partner schools – Hatton Hill Primary School, Dovedale Primary School, St Margaret Mary’s, Northcote Primary School and Rice Lane Primary School – took part.

As the official charitable arm of Everton Football Club, EitC is currently working closely with the NHS to deliver Type 1 diabetes awareness training to staff across its Primary Education partner schools.

Led by Paediatric Diabetes Specialist Nurse Helen Day and Diabetes Educator Michelle Quinn from Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Ormskirk Paediatric Diabetes Team, the sessions aim to help teachers better understand the condition, challenge misconceptions, support pupils living with diabetes and share their knowledge with the wider school community.

Jake joined pupils and staff in a range of interactive activities designed to improve their understanding of the condition. These included exploring a visual body board to learn how the body processes glucose and the role insulin play in regulating blood glucose levels.

Using Virtuali-Tee interactive T-shirts from EitC’s Digital Skills Lab, Jake also engaged with pupils to explore the ‘inside’ of the human body and learn more about the role of the pancreas in producing insulin.

A relaxed Q&A session then gave the 25-year-old footballer the opportunity to share his own experiences of living with Type 1 diabetes, while hearing directly from pupils about how they manage the condition.

Speaking about living with Type 1 diabetes, O’Brien said: “I was diagnosed at the age of 16. I’d been drinking a lot of water, feeling more tired than usual and losing a lot of weight, despite trying hard to gain it.

“My parents took me to the doctors as a precaution, but my blood sugar levels were so high that I was then sent to the hospital and quickly diagnosed there.

“I didn’t know much about the condition and was looking up who else had been diagnosed. I think it’s really important for these young kids to know they can do anything they set their minds to.”

By the end of the 2026/27 season, Everton in the Community aims to have supported the delivery of diabetes awareness and education sessions to staff across all its Primary and Secondary Education partner schools, as well as rolling out children’s awareness sessions to help pupils support their classmates living with Type 1 diabetes.

Primary Stars Senior Coordinator, Elena Barton, added: “Many of our young people living with Type 1 diabetes look up to Jake, so it was really special for them to have the opportunity to meet him, share their experiences and hear about his own journey. One even refers to Jake as his ‘diabetes brother’.

“Our Primary Education team is working closely with teachers across our partner schools to bring diabetes awareness learning to life, providing continuing professional development (CPD) opportunities to help educators better understand how to support pupils living with the condition.

“This is particularly important during physical education lessons, when children's blood glucose levels can fluctuate. We’ve had the training ourselves and now want to share it across our partner school network and beyond.”

To find out more information about Everton in the Community’s diabetes training sessions or get involved with future events, contact Elena at elena.barton@evertonfc.com.

#1441. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admits his newlook team need to deliver sooner rather than later

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a new style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

Asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he said: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  says his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

‘Some new faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’

McGinn also said that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most important part.

‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager said: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

But the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli

‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick said. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. “We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler said. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”

#1438. Fleetwood v Everton Cup Quarter-Final Ticket News

Everton can confirm ticketing arrangements for the Club’s Carabao Cup quarter-final against Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium on Thursday 17 December (8pm GMT kick-off).

The Club has received an allocation of 718 tickets, including six pairs of wheelchair spaces, for the eagerly-anticipated cup tie.

Following Fleetwood Town’s recent sell-out fixture against Arsenal, the League Two club has reviewed its stadium safety arrangements to accommodate operational requirements and maximise ticket availability for home supporters. These adjustments have resulted in a slightly reduced away allocation compared to the previous round but still accounts for just under 15 per cent of Highbury’s capacity.

With the allocation significantly smaller than those received for most Everton Premier League away fixtures, and demand expected to considerably exceed availability, tickets will be distributed through a ballot process.

The Club has previously consulted its fan groups on the fairest approach to allocating tickets for fixtures where demand exceeds availability, including occasions when the number of eligible supporters with maximum away credits is greater than the number of tickets available.

The Club has extended the away credits qualifying period to recognise supporters’ attendance over a longer period, reviewing ticketing data dating back to the 2021/22 season. However, even with an extended period of accumulated away credits, the number of eligible supporters still exceeds the available allocation. For this reason, a ballot process is therefore required.

The ballot will be open to 2026/27 Season Ticket Members who have accumulated 126 away credits across the 2021/22 to 2026/27 seasons, up to and including the Club’s recent away Premier League fixture against Newcastle United.

Supporters can check their qualifying away credit history by clicking here.

Further information on the fixtures included within the qualifying period can be found here.

Official Supporters’ Clubs will also be required to submit applications through the ballot process, with eligible members included in the same ballot as other qualifying supporters. Supporters’ Club members will only be eligible if they meet the required credit criteria.

The Club’s allocation includes seating in the Parkside Stand and standing tickets in the Percy Ronson Stand.

The Supporter Number of every eligible entrant must be provided when submitting a ballot application.

The ballot application window will open at 10am on Thursday 19 November, closing at 4pm on the same day.

Box Office opening times can be found HERE.

Supporters may apply individually or as part of a group of up to six family and friends, provided every member of the group meets the qualifying criteria.

Each supporter or Membership number can only be entered into the ballot once. Supporters included within a group application cannot submit a separate individual application or be included in another group.

All applicants will be notified of the outcome of their ballot application by 4pm on Friday 20 November.

In recognition of the exceptionally limited allocation, and to ensure supporters are not disadvantaged in future away ticket applications, all successful and unsuccessful ballot applicants will still receive an away credit for the fixture. This will be applied to their account once the match has been played.

The Club has received six pairs of wheelchair spaces, which are included within the overall allocation of 718 tickets.

Supporters who require wheelchair accommodation must submit their applications in writing directly to Everton’s Accessibility Team during the Ballot opening timeline (Thursday 19 November between 10am and 4pm). Tickets will be issued to supporters who meet the qualifying criteria based on previous away credit history.

Coach travel costs £35 and will depart from Goodison Park at 4:30pm. Supporters must be Travel Club members to purchase coach tickets. The Travel Club Membership costs just £5.

Everton has also been able to secure a limited number of hospitality packages for this fixture, offering supporters an alternative way to experience the quarter-final at Highbury.

Supporters interested in securing a hospitality package can register their interest by CLICKING HERE.

Supporters are reminded that it is an offence under Section 166 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 for any unauthorised person to resell football tickets.

Further information on the Club’s position regarding ticket touting can be found here.

Watch the quarter-final at Hill Dickinson Stadium

For Evertonians unable to attend the fixture at Highbury Stadium, the Club will host a special live screening of the quarter-final at Kendall’s Social at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Supporters will have the opportunity to come together with fellow Blues at the Club’s waterfront home to watch the action and get behind the team as Everton look to secure a place in the Carabao Cup semi-finals.

For more information on the screening and how to attend, please CLICK HERE.

#1436. Spain 2-3 England PLAYER RATINGS: Which star was the man of the match for Thomas Tuchel? Who was key to their energy and adventure? And who now deserves a run in the side?

Published: 17:06 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:47 EST, 15 November 2026

England secured a historic victory over Spain in the Nations League to secure top spot in their group ahead of their quarter-final matchup next year.

Thomas Tuchel's side raced out the blocks to cause the world champions trouble early on, but Unai Simon ensured Spain held firm and weathered the early storm.

England did get their reward, though, just before half-time when Harry Kane won and scored a penalty to give his side a deserved lead.

After the break, they went up a gear, with Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White netting to leave England in dreamland.

That was until Elliot Anderson was sent off – conceding a penalty against Lamine Yamal in the process – and Spain were back in it through Mikel Oyarzabal. Nico Williams then ensured it would be a nervy last 15 minutes for England, but they held on and secured the 3-2 victory.

Daily Mail Sport's CRAIG HOPE was in Madrid to rate the Three Lions players.

England secured a thrilling 3-2 win over Spain on Sunday to top their Nations League group

James Trafford produced a fantastic double save in stoppage time to keep his side in front

His big test and was hardly tested first-half. That changed when down to 10 and produced three big saves, including a stunner in stoppage-time.

Solid if unspectacular… at least until spectacular, overlapping goal for England’s third. Shades of Carlos Alberto. Warrants a stay in side.

Looked composed until needless dawdling on ball that cost his team a penalty, a goal and a man. Spoilt decent display.

Furthered claims as first-choice centre back. Was commanding, organised well and headed brilliant second goal. Player of the match.

Surely England’s No1 left back now. Two early dribbles were Yamal-esque. A tougher second-half and was out of position for Spain’s second.

Superb ball to free Kane for penalty and was his usual commanding self, until desperate tug on Yamal at expense of penalty and red card.

Elliot Anderson was sent off after bringing down Lamine Yamal in the penalty box at 3-0

Best work was in own half for most part but set-piece deliveries were teasing and accurate, including corner for Konsa goal. A strong showing.

Quieter than star-man display on Thursday but his work was diligent on right and included some classy touches.

Drove England forward second-half and was key to energy and adventure. Won corner for second and assisted third.

More energy and purpose than Croatia, even if killer ball was still missing. An honest shift and played his part.

Showed cunning and class to win and convert first-half penalty. Sacrificed at 2-3 after another masterclass in centre forward play.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin (on for Gordon 83) – 6

At 1-0 up against a top nation (remember Argentina) he kept his side on the front foot and was rewarded, until they went down to 10 men. A big night for the head coach.

Thomas Tuchel kept his side on the front foot when ahead against a top nation and was rewarded until the red card

#1435. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1434. George & Armstrong Start In England Under-21s Friendly

Harrison Armstrong and Tyrique George both played an hour of England Under-21s’ 1-0 defeat to Portugal at Ashton Gate Stadium.

The Young Lions went behind to an Afonso Moreira goal in the 28th minute and were unable to find a way past keeper João Carvalho from there.

This was Armstrong’s first start for the Under-21s after making his debut as a substitute against Ireland in the previous international window, while George was making his 10th appearance at this level.

Lee Carsley’s side had already secured qualification for next summer’s UEFA U21 Euro finals in October, and are using these friendlies in preparation for the tournament in Albania and Serbia.

Armstrong and George return to action in Bristol on Monday 16 November, taking on France (7.30pm kick-off).

#1433. My Story: O’Brien's Diabetes Diagnosis & Journey Into Football

To mark World Diabetes Day, we revisiting a chat with Everton defender Jake O’Brien, who sat down to discuss his experiences with the condition.

A Republic of Ireland international, O'Brien also covered a wide range of topics including his journey into professional football and an impressive sporting background.

O’Brien was diagnosed with type one diabetes aged 16 – and recalling that time, he explained: “There were a few weeks when I was ill. I was losing a lot of weight and was very tired. I was drinking eight or nine litres of water a day.

“I realised something wasn’t right. I went to the doctor’s and they sent me up to hospital and diagnosed me with it. My pancreas, basically, doesn’t work; it doesn’t produce insulin.

"It’s a genetic thing, I suppose, but in that sense, no one in my family has ever had it."

#1432. Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'
