#1359. Switzerland 4-0 Scotland: Swiss stroll leaves serious question marks over Sebastien Pocognoli as Scots round off miserable campaign with defeat on captain Andrew Robertson's record-breaking night

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:06 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:08 EST, 16 November 2026

Despite re-establishing Scotland’s credentials as a credible football nation, by common consent, Steve Clarke’s time in charge of the side was up in the summer.

With qualification for a major tournament no longer satisfying the desires of the Tartan Army, a seven-year itch led to a parting of the ways.

In order to take that elusive step into a knock-out round, the theory went that employing a bolder coach who’d get more out of the players was all that was required. So much for that.

While few would dispute that a change at the helm was required, it was legitimate to question the wisdom in the SFA making one which was quite so radical. Those concerns have only been amplified by what’s been witnessed so far under Sebastien Pocognoli.

The Belgian is young, smart and intense. He won a title in Belgium with Union Saint-Gilloise and will have taken much from his brief, ill-fated spell at Monaco. He wants to play the kind of football supporters long to see.

But this Nations League campaign has been nothing short of dismal. Two wins from six matches, both of those coming against a poor North Macedonia side, and three nights to forget against the Swiss and Slovenia, is a lamentable record.

Andy Robertson endured a miserable night on the occasion of his record-breaking 103rd cap

Notwithstanding the fact that there were always likely to be teething problems, it’s fallen miles short of modest expectations.

Talk of it taking up to 18 months to all come up roses is all very well. But to believe that’s going to be the case, you need to see more green shoots at this point.

Having finished third in the section, Scotland are bound for pot three when the draw for Euro 2028 is made in Belfast next month.

Unless there’s a radical improvement come the qualifiers in March, it’s hard to see how Pocognoli’s side will get there by any means other than the back door.

This was another tough watch for the travelling supporters, one which will only lead to growing concerns about where all this is heading.

For half of a half, Scotland actually looked like they were getting somewhere under their new manager.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli faces some serious questions over a miserable campaign

From the minute Lewis Ferguson scored a horrible own goal, though, they became a rabble. Not nearly enough punch on the front foot. And far too easy to play through.

They shipped two goals inside five minutes early in the second half and looked like they’d have taken the final whistle there and then.

Individual mistakes from players are troubling Pocognoli in the same way they pockmarked the later days of Clarke’s reign.

Having witnessed Grant Hanley, Scott McKenna and Andy Robertson err in the World Cup, the Tartan Army had already seen Jack Hendry sent off against the Swiss at Hampden before Ferguson joined the growing list of sinners here.

Arriving midway through the first half, his unfathomable moment came when there wasn’t a red shirt in close proximity. It was a kick in the teeth for Pocognoli after a reasonable start.

While it would have been stretching matters to suggest that his team were vulnerable, Murat Yakin was without four of his big hitters in Manuel Akanji, Johan Manzambi, Dan Ndoye and Granit Xhaka.

There was a smattering of starters with five or six caps to their name. Two of the front three, Samuel Ballet and Winsley Boteli, were just 20.

Lewis Ferguson can't believe his misfortune after slicing the ball into his own net for the opener

It was a night when Scottish football history was made with Robertson winning his 103rd cap to finally rise above his great friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish.

Pocognoli stuck by the back-three – Ryan Porteous, Luke Graham and Kieran Tierney – who acquitted themselves well against North Macedonia.

There was no great shock that the more defensive-minded Aaron Hickey replaced Ben Gannon-Doak on the right. Without a goal in 21 matches before a ball was kicked, Oli McBurnie’s selection ahead of Che Adams was intriguing.

The infuriating thing from Pocognoli’s perspective was that his side began with the right attitude.

Aside from an Isaac Schmidt shot which was fielded by Angus Gunn, they looked comfortable.

John McGinn’s pass into McBurnie saw the Hull forward flick the ball into space for Hickey to chase. Just when it looked like he might get a shot away, he was caught.

The positive early approach was typified by Porteous flying into a tackle 30 yards from the Swiss goal and winning the ball.

Winsley Boteli enjoys the moment after putting the stylish Swiss two goals ahead on the night

Had it not been for Hickey hesitating to pick out Scott McTominay’s run, the Napoli man would have been in on goal.

To put it mildly, the Swiss didn’t need an invitation to go down. The appropriately named Samuel Ballet was especially fond of the theatrics.

For a brief spell, Scotland had their opponents hemmed in. Pocognoli was miffed that two quick corners didn’t amount to anything.

Billy Gilmour probed and McTominay made key interceptions and sprayed passes. McGinn fired over.

At the midway point in the first half, there was much to admire. Then disaster struck.

The Swiss did well to advance down the right. Zachary Athekame simply launched a cross into the box and hoped for the best.

Aaron Hickey endured a painful injury blow and could now face another spell on the sidelines

With Ferguson running back towards goal and Porteous waiting to boot the ball to safety, there was no obvious danger.

For reasons only he could explain, the Bologna man stretched out a leg and watched on in horror as the ball sailed past Gunn. All that hard work undone in one desperate moment.

Hickey passed up a chance to immediately level when he headed Robertson’s cross wide. It was to be the Brentford man’s last meaningful involvement before he felt his hamstring tighten. Nathan Patterson replaced him.

A gift of a goal gave the Swiss a boost. Boteli launched himself at Alvyn Sanches’ cross. Gunn was untroubled.

Patterson did well to head Robertson’s deep cross back into the danger zone. McGinn’s header was straight into the arms of Yvon Mvogo.

For all Scotland were entitled to feel a little sore at being one down at the break, it could have been worse. The defence were completely static as Adrian Bajrami launched himself at a header. It was a good thing, from Gunn’s point of view, that the defender missed the target.

Alvyn Sanches drills home Switzerland's third goal in what was an entirely one-sided contest

Ferguson truly had a night to forget here. Within two minutes of the restart, he needlessly invited pressure when he launched a ball straight out of play.

Within seconds, with Porteous advanced, the Swiss broke down the left. Ballet fed Remo Freuler who returned the favour. Ballet rolled the ball towards goal from 12 yards with Boteli claiming the final touch. The visitors’ hopes of a VAR reprieve for offside were dashed.

And with that, the roof caved in. Patterson was dispossessed and Boteli worked the ball into the feet of Sanches. You could only admire the finish, but Scotland were an absolute mess in the build-up. It was threatening to get ugly.

With Tierney, Scotland’s best player on the night, lying on the deck, Ballet was only denied by Gunn. The Tartan Army looked at the clock and wished it was over.

With a minute remaining, a bad night got worse when Zeki Amdouni’s deflected shot beat Gunn.

Mercifully, this tortuous Nations League campaign can now be consigned to history. It’s been the most chastening experience for all concerned.

#1358. Marco Materazzi Criticised For Comments About Jesus de Miguel’s Death

It's been just two weeks since the tragic death of CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, who passed away following an on-pitch collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

The 30-year-old was rushed to hospital after the incident, which saw Owono's knee make contact with his chest. However, the Spanish Segunda Division club announced his passing the next morning.

Jesus Owono has broken his silence after the tragic passing of CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono has since been handed a 12-match ban and is contemplating whether he ever wants to return to football. The Spanish police opened an involuntary manslaughter investigation following the tragic events.

Marco Materazzi played just under 500 professional matches during his 25-year career. Of those appearances, 41 came for Italy.

His most significant moment in football was lifting the 2006 World Cup with his country. However, he's not best remembered for the goal he scored in the final against France or his overall contribution to the match itself.

Instead, the first thing that comes to mind for the majority of fans who hear his name is that Zinedine Zidane headbutt. Zizou reportedly took exception to a comment Materazzi made to him during the match and responded by planting his head into the Italian's chest, ending his playing career on a sour note.

Referee Horacio Elizondo has opened up on one of the most iconic moments in World Cup history.

Materazzi has been in the headlines again recently. This time, for comments he made relating to the death of De Miguel. The 53-year-old compared his physical collision with Zidane to the challenge that saw Di Miguel lose his life.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport, he said: "The death of Jesús de Miguel made me thank God that nothing had happened. They're talking about manslaughter for a gambling tactic: what if it had happened to me?"

Those words have been criticised by football fans on social media and have been labelled 'tone-deaf'. One supporter said: "It's so tone-deaf," while another added: "How can I make this about me?"

Another questioned: "Is this not an insane thing to say? Seriously. How self-centred and tone-deaf can you be?" One Reddit user said: "Read the room, Marco."

Another World Cup winner who has given his thoughts on the situation is Gerard Pique. The former Spain and Barcelona defender is now the owner of FC Andorra, Owono's club.

Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera has responded to the sanction given to Jesus Owono for his role in the incident that caused Jesus de Miguel's death.

Responding to the 12-game suspension handed out to the goalkeeper, Pique claimed the sanction placed blame on Owono. He said:

"Why did this happen? Players, former players, coaches, goalkeepers... they’ve all called it an accident. I truly believe that imposing the maximum penalty on Jesús for this incident puts him in a situation he doesn’t deserve, because he isn’t to blame for any of this. My take on all this is that the 12-game suspension for Jesús Owono seems to me to be placing the blame on Jesús for consequences that weren’t his fault. I believe the penalty should be based on the action itself, not on the consequences."

Statistics in this article are courtesy of Transfermarkt. Correct as of 18-11-26.

#1357. The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

This is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

Erling Haaland gives Manchester City the lead against Liverpool 🎯 https://t.co/cELo5y60Fk

In fact, Liverpool’s best performers were the young attackers Victor Muñoz and, making his first league start as a makeshift centre-forward, Lewis Koumas, who is just 21. Against that, City unleashed a battery of forward talent.

"Koumas & Munoz were better than the two £100million players!" Jamie Carragher is still disappointed with what he's seeing from Florian Wirtz in a Liverpool shirt 😬🔴 https://t.co/jJwOZbPJ4b

Was it an unfair advantage? It appears City have been thriving off that for some time and, while this team were not signed during the years the club have been found guilty of cheating, the argument is, of course, that they would not have joined without the sporting supremacy.

Certainly not Haaland, despite his avowed love for City. That cannot be doubted as his father, Alf-Inge, a former midfielder for the club, stood celebrating in the away end. The striker missed one chance when he should have scored, sent through on goal, shaking his head in disbelief at getting his angles wrong. It felt like a warning and that went unheeded as Doku, who had replaced one of their big summer signings in Iliman Ndiaye, cut in from the left with his shot deflecting into Haaland’s path. He made no mistake with a powerful, first-time finish.

Doku soon added a second, a sublime strike, as he dribbled goalwards, defenders backing off, and he arced a right-footed shot high beyond Alisson Becker’s grasp.

There were delighted chants of “olé” from the City supporters and that arrogance was rewarded by a strutting, emphatic third goal. It was finished by the mercurial Rayan Cherki after he was sent clear by a backheel from Josko Gvardiol, another substitute.

A moment of individual brilliance from Rayan Cherki to put the game beyond all doubt 🤯 https://t.co/wvmTMZcGhW

It captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. In a sea of uncertainty as to what will now happen, that is something we can be sure of.

“Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Those signs of defiance were not matched on the pitch. Although it may be a song City will get used to hearing for the rest of this extraordinary, unprecedented campaign.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”

Maresca said City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

“The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”

The Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

“The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”

City motor forward on the counter through Cherki, whose delightful touch takes him away from Mac Allister. From inside his own half, the Frenchman dribbles to the edge of Liverpool’s penalty area. He attempts to play a one-two with Fernandez, but the pass is cut out by Jacquet.

Manchester City have not got going, as of yet. The defiant message from the club is they would not let the verdict affect them. They have defended well enough but have barely strung a passing sequence together against a Liverpool side who appear be playing off pure emotion.

Gravenberch is bossing this game in midfield. Another powerful run from deep results in a delightful nutmeg on Fernandez, who slips over. Liverpool’s energy has been really impressive. City need to ride out this early storm.

Inflatable bananas to signify nostalgia for the late 1980s, when these were all the rage after the club’s relegation to Division Two? A re-imagining of Oasis’ Wonderwall at the front of the Kop. “And after all,” the banner reads, “you really robbed us all.”

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission said. I think that’s what’s worried me.”

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

#1356. Napoli sign agreement to purchase land for new state-of-the-art training centre

Napoli President Aurelio De Laurentiis has confirmed that he has signed a preliminary agreement to purchase up to 18 hectares of land to build a new state-of-the-art training centre in the Qualiano area of Naples, with work scheduled to get underway in early 2027.

De Laurentiis took to social media on Wednesday afternoon to share images of the signing of the contracts, along with the message: “It’s done, full steam ahead.”

According to Sky Sport Italia, Napoli have agreed to purchase 13 hectares of land in Qualiano with an option for an additional five hectares.

The new Napoli training ground project will include eight pitches, plus two more if they acquire the additional five hectares, a specialist goalkeeping facility, a small stadium for youth team matches, reception and lounge areas for players and staff, office spaces and a pond that will provide water for pitch irrigation.

The works are expected to get underway in early 2027. There are still a few bureaucratic steps to undertake first, though, including gaining formal permission to build upon the plot, which is currently designated as agricultural land.

“Napoli has always had its home in Castel Volturno, where we won two league titles,” De Laurentiis told reporters on Wednesday.

“Have you seen where Maradona trained? Today is definitely a new beginning, because we have completed the first phase and now we can move onto the second.”

#1355. Sky Sports: Man Utd Plotting £67m Move for Newcastle Star Malick Thiaw

Manchester United are looking to bolster their defensive ranks in 2027, and a new target has emerged as a possibility for Mauricio Pochettino.

The Argentine has replaced Michael Carrick as the boss at Old Trafford this week, and will lead the team into a new era, with a defensive rebuild planned for the new year in both January and the summer.

Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Lisandro Martinez are all out of contract at the end of the current campaign, and it seems unlikely that any of them will be staying at the club beyond this season. New arrivals are expected to take their place, and the club are once again looking at Premier League players who can come in to make an instant impact.

A number of central defenders have been linked with a January move to the club, including Brentford captain Nathan Collins and Fulham star Calvin Bassey.

But it seems United are in contact with a number of players at the Unique Sports Group agency, who represent Bassey, as a report by Sky Sports Germany states that the club are also showing a strong interest in Newcastle United star Malick Thiaw.

The 25-year-old joined the Magpies in the summer of 2025 from AC Milan in a deal worth around £30m, and immediately established himself as a key player. His status in the squad was cemented this summer, when he was appointed into the club's leadership group, and he has worn the captain's armband on a number of occasions this season.

Thiaw is now valued at £67m by Newcastle, but it's reported that a summer exit in 2027 has not been ruled out, with Man Utd among the most interested parties for his signature.

Regarded as the 'undisputed leader' of the defence at St James' Park, the club do not want to lose him, but accept that they may be forced to sell for a big fee if Champions League clubs come calling, and they are unable to turn their slow start to the season around.

The 6ft 4 star has also recently broken into the Germany first-team, with Jurgen Klopp understood to be a huge fan of his qualities. His current contract is due to expire in 2029.

Man Utd need defensive reinforcements, and so it's no surprise that a number of players are going to start being linked with a move to Old Trafford as a result.

INEOS have shown that they prefer to shop in the Premier League since taking over, and Thiaw would fit that. He is also just 25 and has his prime years ahead of him, while he has the experience of playing for a big club like AC Milan in his career too.

But with Newcastle likely to demand a huge fee to let him leave, the Red Devils could surely find a player of comparable quality for a much lesser fee, and free up funds to make other signings instead.

Thiaw has his qualities, but we have seen him exposed in the Premier League before. Until there is a leader and proven starter in the backline to help guide him along, United would be making a huge gamble by spending such big money on bringing him in at this stage of their rebuild under Pochettino.

United simply cannot afford to get their signings wrong at this stage, and with Newcastle certain to play hardball for any deal, they'd be better off looking elsewhere unless they are 100% convinced he is the right man for the role and the new manager.

Manchester United chiefs are ready to back Mauricio Pochettino in the transfer market

#1352. Leeds Ditched Star Labelled ‘Worse Than Augustin’, Now He’s Scored 11 CL Goals

Leeds United have made some excellent signings in recent years, none more so than current club captain Ethan Ampadu, as well as England duo James Trafford and Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Ampadu has taken the jump from the Championship to the Premier League like a duck to water, while Trafford and Calvert-Lewin both have the quality to take Leeds to the next level after they consolidated their spot in the top flight in the first season after promotion.

Calvert-Lewin is even attracting interest from rivals Manchester United but, according to GIVEMESPORT sources, he is set to extend his contract to stay at Elland Road instead.

It's fair to say that, like many clubs, the Yorkshire outfit haven't always got it right with their transfer business.

There are already big doubts over summer addition Jean-Matteo Bahoya, who was viewed as an exciting signing but who has barely been picked by Daniel Farke, with the club already making a decision on terminating his loan spell in the January transfer window.

Bahoya isn't the only forward to be a flop, so far at least, at Elland Road in recent years, with Facundo Buonanotte and Jean-Kevin Augustin two more prime examples.

Leeds signed the former on loan from Brighton and Hove Albion in January of this year to boost their survival battle, but he played just 36 minutes of Premier League football between then and the end of the campaign, before returning to the Seagulls.

The story of Augustin is even more interesting, from a player who signed on loan from RB Leipzig, to one who ended up costing the Whites around £40m, despite playing only 48 minutes of football for them.

Leeds signed Augustin on loan with a £18m obligation to buy the player if they won promotion to the Premier League, although they argued that, because the Championship season had been interrupted due to the coronavirus pandemic and not completed until July, Augustin's contract should have reverted to Leipzig at the time they actually went up.

Leeds lost their appeal and agreed on a £15.5m compensation package with Leipzig, while they were also ordered to pay Augustin himself £24.5m in compensation because of the failed permanent transfer.

Augustin will undoubtedly go down as Leeds' worst ever signing for that reason and the number of minutes paid, but Leeds content creator Joe Wainman told GIVEMESPORT previously that Weston McKennie was 'arguably worse than Augustin'.

He said: "The mad thing is, I'm that vitriolic towards last season and the demise of the football club, with the poor acquisitions that we made and the coach that was in charge made in Jesse Marsch, that I would say with chest that Weston McKennie is arguably a worse signing than JKA, and JKA played about 15 minutes.

That's how strongly I feel about that. He seemed disinterested. We saw nowhere near the player that he's shown in the past, as you've mentioned.

That is a big statement that might have been in the heat of the moment, but there was no doubt that McKennie was a big disappointment at Elland Road.

Leeds signed the USA international on loan in January 2023 until the end of the season, with the option to make the deal permanent for ££30m.

Speaking on his arrival, McKennie when asked what he was going to bring, said: "Hard work, non-stop 90 minutes back and forth, tackles, trash talk probably and everything - funny moments and serious moments.

It's a dream come true, I've dreamed of playing in the Premier League for the longest time. To have the support system I have here, I'm ready.

Some Leeds fans would certainly question the work-rate they saw from the American in the final months of the season, as they were relegated from the Premier League and McKennie returned to his parent club.

Having failed to reach the levels he had done earlier in his career during his time in Yorkshire, it would have been a surprise to supporters that his career has continued on an upward trajectory, with the 28-year-old establishing himself as a key player for Juve.

McKennie scored nine goals and registered eight assists for the Serie A giants last term, including netting four times in the Champions League, taking his career total in the competition to 11.

McKennie may not be a well-loved figure at Leeds after the role he played in their demise that season, but he has shown the quality he has in his locker, which makes his Elland Road spell even more disappointing.

Leeds are ready to add a new forward to their frontline in the January transfer window

#1351. Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1,2,3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex–antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a new and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials.

#1350. 'One to Watch' - Ben Jacobs: Man Utd Could Move to Sign Gusto for Pochettino

Manchester United could potentially be one of the busiest clubs in the January transfer window as they look to give new manager Mauricio Pochettino what he needs to turn the club's season around, with GIVEMESPORT senior correspondent Ben Jacobs naming a France international as one possible target.

Hopes were high of another strong season for Man United under the permanent leadership of Michael Carrick after their rise up the Premier League table in the first half of 2026, but instead they have made a miserable start to the campaign.

The Red Devils have won just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches this term, while losing three of their five fixtures in the EFL Cup and Champions League too, which has left them in the relegation places in the top flight.

It could get even worse for them this weekend, as they could be bottom of the table by the time they kick off in Pochettino's first match against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

That will happen if Crystal Palace win in Thomas Frank's first game in charge against Coventry City, and Sunderland draw with Aston Villa.

Pochettino knows he has a big task ahead to turn United's fortunes around, and especially from a defensive point of view, where they have conceded four goals against Como and Aston Villa, and three against Bournemouth, in their previous five fixtures.

GIVEMESPORT sources have revealed that club chiefs will look at signing a new striker in January, with Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin one player they are keen on, although the England international looks likely to sign a new contract at Elland Road instead.

Meanwhile, in his latest GMS newsletter, Jacobs has confirmed that United are also looking at the centre-back and full-back positions, with Chelsea's Malo Gusto 'one to watch'.

On the right hand side, even though maybe a right-sided full-back is not as high a priority as a left-sided one, Malo Gusto could be one to watch.

"There’s been no contact between Manchester United and Gusto yet, and Manchester City have looked in the past as well. But Chelsea are prepared to sell at the right price.

“Over the summer, that number was £75million and it would have to be dropped significantly, you would imagine anyway, if anyone’s going to come in for the France International, but more broadly, Gusto’s future is one to watch in this January window."

While United may not want to pay £75m to sign Gusto, especially given Chelsea are willing to sell him if the price is right, a move for the 23-year-old would also make a lot of sense.

The France international has already played under Pochettino, with the duo together at Stamford Bridge from the summer of 2023 to when the Argentine was sacked in May 2024.

Gusto knows how the 54-year-old wants to play and should be able to make an immediate impact in a Pochettino team as a result, while he also boasts 100 Premier League appearances and Champions League experience too.

Most impressive though is Gusto's versatility, as while his primary position is as a right-back or right wing-back, he has also been used as a left-back and even in midfield during his career.

It's no secret that United were looking for left-back competition for Luke Shaw in the summer, having shown strong interest in Newcastle United's Lewis Hall and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, although neither move materialised as they prioritised signing three central midfielders.

Signing Gusto could kill two birds with one stone if he is seen as a player who can perform well in both roles, although there will of course be some caution given Diogo Dalot is a player who can play left-back and right-back, but has largely ultimately struggled when deployed on his weaker side.

Gusto has 17 caps for France and a big future ahead, and if United were able to secure him for a lower fee than the summer asking price, it could be a smart addition to help Pochettino.

Manchester United chiefs are ready to back Mauricio Pochettino in the transfer market

#1349. Carnevali: ‘Juventus unable to make significant investments on players, it’s a challenge’

Juventus CEO Giovanni Carnevali has admitted that it is difficult for the club to invest heavily on new signings due to their UEFA settlement agreement and says that this is a result of mistakes that have been made in previous seasons: ‘I have plenty of confidence, but it takes time’.

Carnevali spoke to the media on Wednesday after an appearance at the RCS Sport Industry Talk in Milan.

Carnevali says that in order to achieve sporting results, clubs are required to invest heavily in their playing staff, but says that this is difficult for Juventus at the moment as a result of the settlement agreement they signed with UEFA back in July.

Juventus were found to have broken the football earnings rule, which allows a maximum aggregate deficit of €60m across a period of three financial years, which for Juventus, covered 2023, 2024 and 2025.

As a result, Juve were handed a conditional fine of up to €20m, at least €6m of which is guaranteed, and signed a three-year settlement agreement that requires them to meet strict financial targets set out by the European governing body. Full details of the settlement agreement are available on the UEFA website.

Carnevali discussed the complications that the settlement agreement has brought to Juventus on Wednesday.

“Today, our main difficulty relates to the settlement agreement,” said Carnevali (via Sky). “If we want to make significant investments on players, we find we are unable to do so. It’s a challenge because in order to achieve sporting results, you need to invest in great players.

“The club has carried out a capital injection, which means that we have made some mistakes in past years. I have plenty of confidence, but it takes time.”

Carnevali added: “Being at Juventus is a source of pride. It’s a forward-thinking club. If we’re talking about Juve, we’re talking about the stadium that we own, about JHotel, about JMedical. Over the years, Juventus has always tried to look ahead, thinking about opportunities that extend beyond football.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

So why don’t you try and bring players through the youth system instead of wasting what little money you do have on rubbish?

#1348. Le Tissier Tipped Him As Southampton's Next Lallana, Now He Plays Non-League Football

In the last 50 years, Southampton are widely recognised as having one of the best academies in football.

From bringing through the likes of Matthew Le Tissier and Alan Shearer in the 1980s, to Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and James Ward-Prowse in more recent years, Southampton have made a lot of money through player sales.

As well as Le Tissier and Shearer, considered to be two of the greatest Premier League players of all time, Gareth Bale and Theo Walcott are two more players from the academy who went on to play at the highest level for Real Madrid and Arsenal.

Luke Shaw was another who came through the ranks before joining Manchester United, where he still is 13 years later, and Calum Chambers was another who left St Mary's for Arsenal after breaking through under Mauricio Pochettino.

It's fair to say that those success stories have dried up a little in more recent years, while the club has spent more time battling at the bottom of the Premier League and in the Championship, with a number of players failing to make the grade having made first-team appearances.

Striker Sam Gallagher left for Blackburn Rovers in 2019, Matt Targett joined Aston Villa after a 15-year association with the south coast outfit, while Harrison Reed signed for Fulham after failing to break into the midfield at St Mary's.

Two of the more recent rare success stories are Tyler Dibling, who joined Everton for a huge fee in the summer of 2025, and Jimmy-Jay Morgan, who is currently scoring for fun at West Bromwich Albion after leaving Saints for Chelsea as a 17-year-old.

Southampton have had other young players who looked on course for a big future at St Mary's too, especially following their U21 Premier League Cup win against Blackburn in 2015.

After watching the final live, Saints legend Le Tissier was asked by Sky Sports to pick out five youngsters to watch who had first-team potential, and he selected Gallagher, Targett, Reed and Sam McQueen.

Le Tissier was particularly complimentary about his final pick, Jake Hesketh, who joined Saints' academy at the age of 10 having been born in Stockport.

He reminds me of Adam Lallana in the way he plays. He's got good feet, moves with the ball really well, and is very, very natural.

"However, he's got a bit of growing and strengthening to do and it won't be an instant thing for him to break through to senior level."

It turned out that Le Tissier may have been right, about his warning over Hesketh.

The teenager was actually promoted to the first-team by Ronald Koeman during the 2014-15 season because of injury issues, and he made his debut for the club in a 2-1 home defeat to Manchester United in December.

Hesketh made a further top flight appearance against Burnley, but he then fell back down the pecking order until Claude Puel was appointed as Koeman's successor in 2016.

He made two further appearances under the Frenchman, scoring his first senior goal in a League Cup tie against Crystal Palace in September 2016, and he also played in the Europa League tie away against Hapoel Be'er Sheva.

The attacking midfielder then picked up an injury and even though he signed a new four-and-a-half year contract in December 2016, he never wore the Southampton shirt again.

He spent time on loan at Burton Albion, MK Dons, Lincoln City and Crawley Town, before leaving St Mary's on a permanent basis for Eastleigh in 2021 after 17 years with the club.

Following two seasons with the National League outfit, Hesketh remained in the Southampton area when he joined Southern League Premier Division club Sholing FC, where he still plays to this day.as a 30-year-old.

The former Southampton star was on the wrong side of the law after leaving St Mary's

#1347. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1346. Conte admits he thinks will return to Juventus and names two times he could have

Antonio Conte says he believes that he will end up back at Juventus as head coach one day and has named two instances over the last few years when he could have returned as head coach of the Bianconeri: ‘I know that eventually the circle will be closed’.

Conte, in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio, has spoken about his connection with Juventus and his willingness to return and ‘close the circle’ with the club where he spent over a decade as a player and won three Scudetti as a head coach.

As a head coach, Conte won three back-to-back league titles in Turin, the first in the club’s run of nine consecutive Scudetti in the 2010s, and Juventus is still the only club where Conte has lasted any longer than two years in charge during his managerial career.

“I think that sooner or later the circle will close,” Conte confessed in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio, which was teased on Wednesday.

“I know I left something behind and I know that eventually the circle will be closed with Juventus.

“There have been moments in the past where we could have reunited, but it’s been difficult because two things have to align. I have to be available and Juventus have to be looking for a coach who isn’t currently employed.”

Conte went on to pinpoint the two moments where he could have returned as head coach of Juventus.

“There have been two instances. Once, when Juventus decided to hire Maurizio Sarri, I was available and later ended up at Inter.

“Then there was a second time when I was free, just as Giuntoli arrived. Giuntoli decided to go for Motta and I went to Napoli.”

Conte also revealed that he had been on the verge of becoming head coach of Juventus in 2009, two years before he was actually appointed. He says that he was in the building and prepared to sign with the Old Lady just before leaving Bari, but a disagreement over the use of Diego saw the deal collapse.

Conte explained: “After my time at Bari, there was a possibility of my going to Juventus. I spoke several times with Castagnini and Secco, Ranieri was the head coach at the time, but eventually they let him go and brought in Ciro [Ferrara] for the final three matches, hoping to qualify for the Champions League.

“They knew perfectly well that I would have played a 4-2-4 formation, given that I would have had forwards like Mauri, Iaquinta, Trezeguet and Del Piero. I told them ‘look, as far as forwards go, we’re all set, we need to sign some wingers’. But for whatever reason, they ended up signing Diego from Werder Bremen instead, and then they called me.

“I remember that it was around the time of the Champions League final between Manchester United and Barcelona in Rome. They called me and said ‘look, we need you to come in because we still need some reassurances from you’. I was still at Bari at the time.

“Anyway, I went, walking in as the Juve manager and then we started talking. They asked me how I wanted to play, and I replied ‘with a 4-2-4’. They said ‘right, but where would you play Diego?’. I answered ‘look, you were the ones who signed him, even though I said that we already have four forwards. So I would play him alongside one of the strikers’.

“Then they told me ‘well, Diego wants to play in a 4-3-1-2’. Imagine my madness at the time. Although, that madness shows that I’m a very direct person who doesn’t make compromises. Anyone else, literally anyone else, would have said ‘sure, I’ll even play him in goal if you want, just let me sign the contract and I’ll join Juve’.

“I was moving from Bari to Juventus after all. But once they said that to me, I stood firm in my ideas, firm in my convictions, and firm in the fact that I wasn’t going to make any compromises or promise anything I knew I wouldn’t deliver.

“So, I told them ‘if a player decides how we play, then I’m not the right coach for you’. And that was it. I walked away and by the time I left that meeting, I was no longer the coach of Juventus.”

#1345. Push it to the Max! Dowman, 16, becomes England U21s youngest-ever goalscorer - as Arsenal starlet scores 89th-minute winner against France

Published: 18:36 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:37 EST, 16 November 2026

Max Dowman broke another record as the 16-year-old became the youngest-ever goalscorer for England's Under-21 side on Monday night.

The Arsenal teenager has already broken a plethora of records at club level, and is now taking that to the international stage too, breaking a record set by senior team star Jude Bellingham, who scored aged 17 years and 67 days in 2020.

Dowman was called into the U21 squad for the first time this international break, and made his debut off the bench in the 1-0 defeat by Portugal on Friday.

On Monday, meanwhile, he was given a start by manager Lee Carsley, and rewarded his manager's faith with an 89th-minute winner to break the record and earn his side a 3-2 win.

It's a record he can add to his already-extensive collection, which includes being the youngest Champions League player, the youngest Premier League goalscorer, and the youngest Premier League winner.

Manager Lee Carsley said after the game: 'He played really well - he was one of four or five outstanding performances. Mikey Moore, Max, Ethan (Nwaneri), they were very good.

Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goal scorer when he scored against France on Monday

'We see how good on the ball he is but he was outstanding off the ball. You have to keep reminding yourself about his age. There's a lot of expectation around him and he seems to handle that so well.

'It's important we keep supporting him and he develops at his own pace. It's so important he enjoys his football.

'Obviously all the players in the squad are under pressure from their clubs and the expectation that surrounds them, so as much as we can we have to make that as easy as we can.'

Despite bursting onto the scene last season, Dowman has just 19 minutes to his name in the top flight this campaign as Arsenal look to defend their title.

He has played a number of games for the Gunners' U21 side, while he was sent off against League Two side Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup.

Arteta scolded his player at the time, but said: 'I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. Whether that's positive or negative. You need to understand the context, the relationship I have with him and what we discussed before we went out.

'If you see the reaction from my mother and father with me sometimes, you'd say "you don't like that reaction", but for me it was the best reaction ever as it enabled me to be who I am.

The Arsenal teenager, 16, broke the record held by Jude Bellingham with his late winner

'But you want to see the best and most beautiful reaction. You want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with 10 men.

'What do you expect? That's the level and that's the reaction. Whether it's right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, I'm f****d off, big time.

'This is the environment and the reality. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League. We look after him so much but we are also demanding as he needs to earn the right to play otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me?'

#1344. JJ Gabriel: Spanish Media Cast Strong Verdict on Man Utd Youngster

JJ Gabriel hasn't even kicked a ball for any of Real Madrid's teams yet and the former Manchester United starlet has already made an impression on Spanish media.

The 16-year-old stunned United when he asked to leave the club in September, and he became the most in-demand teenage talent in the months that followed. As soon as the news dropped that he wanted out of Old Trafford without even making a senior appearance, the likes of Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Manchester City were all linked.

Madrid eventually won the race to sign Gabriel, a move still to be completed and one that confused United's fans because of his supposed wish for regular senior football. His family, including his father, are thought to believe he is a similar superstar talent as Lamine Yamal, but he might have to work hard convincing the Spanish media that he's the real deal.

Gabriel bid farewell to United with a social media post this week, confirming his departure with a video that veteran players often use when wishing fans an emotional goodbye after lengthy stays at clubs. Given that the England youngster didn't even feature for the club's first-team, it caused a stir not only at Old Trafford.

Spanish commentator Juanma Castano discussed the video during an appearance on El Partidazo de Cope and he reacted in astonishment. Pointing out a lack of prominence while at United, he said:

"I say this with the slight fear that this kid might go on to become the greatest player of all time. But it’s just unbelievable. This lad hasn’t played a single minute for Manchester United. Yet he’s said goodbye as if he were a United legend."

Castano added: "Someone leaving the club, the sort of player whose departure would have people in Manchester in tears." He explained that Gabriel is just "a 16-year-old kid who hasn’t even made his debut. He’s a prospect."

When Gabriel pushed to leave United, questions arose about his attitude and those advising him at this stage of his career. Jamie Carragher particularly warned about the influence family can have on a youth prospect and demanding too much, too soon.

Castano echoed this when explaining his concerns about Gabriel and his mindset. He believes that the English winger isn't "what he’s being led to believe he is" and that will lead to “difficulties this boy will face, believing he’s already a football star.”

The Spaniard's colleague, Manolo Lama, has partially blamed the media for building Gabriel up as a superstar in the making at the age of 16:

"We in the media are largely to blame for this. Every week, I see young players, 14 or 15-year-olds, at Real Madrid. Some go on to succeed, others don’t. But we almost always attribute far more value to them than they actually possess."

He added: “Just pick up any newspaper. Every day you’ll find a ‘diamond’ from somewhere or a ‘gem’ from somewhere else.”

Gabriel caught the eye throughout his journey through United's youth ranks, putting in dazzling displays that had the UK press believing him to be Carrington's biggest talent in decades. That included handing him the nickname 'Kid Messi' and constantly reporting on his ventures such as his major sponsorship deal with Nike.

United have yet to even confirm Gabriel's exit and, from their perspective, the club did all they could to convince him to stay and sign a new contract. They are frustrated to have lost one of their academy's most exciting teenagers, but there are others whom they hold in high regard.

Take for example, Shea Lacey, who, unlike Gabriel, has broken into the senior team and has already won over fans with cameo appearances. The 19-year-old came off the bench to set Matheus Cunha up in a 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma in the Champions League earlier this month.

The Red Devils don't have to worry about Noah Ajayi's future as the German starlet signed his first long-term professional contract with the club in September. Gabriel got most of the plaudits for the U18's last season but Ajayi was equally important in attack under Darren Fletcher.

Tynan Thompson is another name United will be hoping can fulfill his potential after forking out an initial £4 million to sign the 18-year-old from Tottenham Hotspur. The English winger may well be viewed as Gabriel's like-for-like replacement at youth level and a talent who could step up to the senior level like Ayden Heaven.

United's main concern right now should be about their first-team struggles that have led to the sacking of Michael Carrick. Mauricio Pochettino has replaced him and the Argentine's first match back in the Premier League is a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday (November 22nd).

#1343. Where Italy stand in FIFA World Rankings after latest international fixtures

Italy will end the calendar year in 14th place in the FIFA World Rankings following a 3-1 victory at home against France and a 4-1 defeat away against Belgium in the Nations League during the November international break.

Italy began the November international break rated as the 15th best national team in the world.

The 3-1 victory at home against France temporarily saw the Azzurri rise up to 13th, but the latest update to the FIFA Men’s World Rankings, which arrived on Thursday, sees them drop back down to 14th following the completion of the latest round of international fixtures.

There have been no changes to the top four-ranked national teams since the start of the November international break: World Cup winners Spain remain top of the rankings despite their recent defeat against England, World Cup finalists Argentina remain in second, France are still in third despite their defeat against Italy and England remain in fourth.

Morocco have risen two places in the rankings up to fifth, Portugal have dropped down one place to sixth, Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil have also dropped one place down to seventh, Belgium remain in eighth place, the Netherlands remain in ninth and Colombia have risen one place to complete the top 10.

Currently ahead of Italy in the rankings are Germany in 11th (up two places), Switzerland in 12th and Mexico in 13th (down three places).

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Immediately after the Win against France, Italy rose to 12th Rank (+3) and not 13th. After the Loss against Belgium, Italy dropped by two Ranks.

#1342. Ryan Giggs Named Two British Stadiums With the Best Atmospheres He’s Seen

No player in the history of the Premier League has made more appearances for Manchester United than Ryan Giggs and he 'won the lot' as their proud Stretford End so eloquently put it.

During Giggs' legendary career, he became the most decorated footballer not only to wear a United shirt but also in English football. The Welshman got his hands on 34 major trophies, 13 league titles and was part of the team that won the treble in 1999.

The unfortunate thing about time in football is that the heroes of yesteryear are quickly forgotten, and the younger generation certainly don't seem to realise just how incredibly talented Giggs was. Most weren't even alive when he glided his way through Arsenal at Highbury to score the most famous FA Cup goal in history and many may have even missed his exploits in Moscow against Chelsea in 2008.

Giggs carved out a career only one can dream of and that meant travelling the globe to play against the very best teams on the planet. He experienced some of the most hostile crowds in world football but the atmosphere at two stadiums particularly left their mark on him.

Giggs played in some of the most heated rivalries in British football, including feisty clashes with Liverpool at Anfield. As enthralling as those fixtures can be, they pale in comparison to the derby between Celtic and Rangers.

Back in 2018, Giggs admitted that he wished to have sampled the atmosphere of an Old Firm Derby having spent his entire career at Old Trafford. Speaking to the Daily Record, he said: "I was talking to Declan John last year about coming up for the Old Firm but he has gone now. It’s something I’ve always wanted to experience."

Giggs added: "There’s no Welsh players in Scotland at the moment unfortunately but it’s something I am definitely keen to do. I’ll get there at some point because everyone I speak to who has been there says it’s unreal. I have played in Glasgow."

The former United winger played seven times against Celtic and Rangers in Champions League competition, stepping out on the Ibrox and Parkhead pitches. Those outings seemed to whet his appetite to attend a derby game:

"Those were amazing atmospheres, probably up there with the best atmospheres I played in."

Giggs even recalled a trip to Turkey but insisted Glasgow was in a league of its own: "I remember going to Turkey in the early days against Galatasaray and it was ferocious but going to Glasgow surpassed that for intensity. I played at Ibrox in the Champions League when Phil Neville scored and a couple of times against Celtic."

He added: "We drew one and lost one. I managed to score in the draw. The noise was incredible. When that Champions League music went on and the crowd got behind the team, it was amazing. You didn’t just have to face 11 men, you had to face those passionate crowds as well."

Giggs's former United teammate Wayne Rooney not only wanted to taste an Old Firm Derby but to do so as a Celtic player. The former England striker revealed he had wished to have played for the Bhoys at some stage of his career.

When Giggs hung up his boots in May 2014, he didn't step into punditry like many of his former teammates nor did he leave Old Trafford. He instead took up an assistant coaching role, first as a player-manager in David Moyes' team before taking charge as caretaker manager and eventually assisting Louis van Gaal.

Some expected him to become permanent boss but instead he's watched Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Michael Carrick try their luck in the dugout. He did, however, land the Wales national team job, spending four years in the role before resigning in 2022.

Giggs' personal life has meant he hasn't been back in football management since, but before he managed his country, he landed on Celtic's radar. In 2016, the Scottish club were looking to replace Ronny Delia and the Welshman was a shock name added to their managerial shortlist.

The Manchester United legend named one famous British stadium as having the best atmosphere he ever experienced as a player.

That came while he assisted Van Gaal and The Daily Mail claim that he had reservations about moving to Scotland. If he had decided to take charge at Parkhead, he'd have been able to experience the Old Firm Derby as a manager, potentially even coming up against his former Liverpool foe Steven Gerrard, who became Rangers boss two years' later.
